newsitem.title: USA: Latest U.S. House tax offer has $10 airline fee.
newsitem.headline: Latest U.S. House tax offer has $10 airline fee.

text.p: The latest House tax offer to the Senate proposed a $10 international arrival and departure fee for airline passengers, a copy of the offer showed Friday.

That provision had been in the original House tax bill but was bumped up to a $15.50 fee when the legislation went through the House Ways and Means Committee. Currently there is a $6 per passenger international departure fee.
The proposal was the latest volley in negotiations between the House and Senate aimed at crafting one final tax bill from their separate versions.
The House offer would retain current law related to flights to and from Alaska and Hawaii and extend those rules to all "U.S. possessions."
The House offer showed agreement on extending current taxes on noncommercial aviation gasoline and jet fuel.
The House also proposed going along with the Senate provision on providing a uniform excise tax on vaccines.
